newsitem.title: USA: Campbell says Heinz dispute set for Camden.
newsitem.headline: Campbell says Heinz dispute set for Camden.

text.p: A legal dispute between Cambell Soup Co and H.J. Heinz Co over Heinz's hiring of a top executive from the rival soup company will be heard at U.S. District Court in Camden, a Campbell spokesman said.

Campbell spokesman Kevin Lowery said a U.S. District Court judge in Camden ruled on Wednesday the case would be heard there, rather than in a state court near Heinz's headquarters in Pittsburgh, as Heinz had sought.
Lowery also said mediation over Heinz's hiring of Daniel O'Neill, the former head of Campbell's U.S. soup division, had failed to yield a settlement.
"It clearly has not been successful and our position is we are prepared to try this case," he said.
Campbell contends O'Neill is bound by a non-competitive agreement and cannot work for Heinz.
Heinz hired O'Neill to head its pet food and Star-Kist tuna operations, and has said the job would not compete with Campbell businesses.
A hearing on Campbell's request for a preliminary injunction to block O'Neill from working for Heinz has been scheduled for February 3, Lowery said.
